This was held over the old course from Mitcham to Brighton and Jack Brown put us in the lead on the first stage.Bill Lucas dropped to 3rd on the next leg only for Stan Gawler to pick up a place on the third relay.
The handicap was won by Mike Stearman (4.30) with Stan Gawler (3.30) 2nd and D.
Peter Bagnall ran a very good race to finish 7th, then came Jim Masters 18th, Bob Taylor 21st, D. Briggs 28th, S.
Next was the Senior Race with a huge field. Our first man home was Jim Masters 21st, followed by Stan Gawler 29th D.

Bedford,our junior D.Baulch,L.Herbert Bill Lucas, Dennis Brickwood, Len Bishop, Eddie Short, S. Gawler and Mike Stearman all of whom were to give the selectors some head aches when trying to find the best team for the approaching National Brighton Relay.
Stan Gawler carried on the good work and also returned the fastest time of the day on his stage and in so doing he brought us back to second place.

Our next two home were Stan Gawler 98th, and Eddie Short 128th.Both these runners were further back than expected, although in fairness to Eddie Short it must be stated that his training has been interrupted this winter.

This saw us as usual at three different venues on the same afternoon the first being at Maidenhead where, in the local 10 miles we provided the winner in Chas Walker in 54m. 57s and who was fairly well backed up by Stan Gawler 6th in 56.35 and E.
